about: The spin-drum carrier as data, built by tools/carrier-v2.mjs from design/carrier-v2.design.json (see design/SHIP-DESIGN.md and design/CARRIER-REBUILD.md). Metres, the ship's frame (x starboard, y up, -z the bow), the ship's axis at x = 0, y = 0. `compartments` are the fixed, weightless hull (grip shoes; down is -y); `drum` holds the spinning rooms, each in its own segment's frame. Do not edit by hand: change the design or the generator and run it again. The first carrier is ships/carrier-v1.layout.json (carrier.html?ship=v1).
name: Twin-drum carrier

drum.about: The spin drums. Two halves in one fixed armoured sleeve, spinning opposite ways about the ship's axis (z). Each half is one ring of `sides` flat-floored segments; segment k is turned 2πk/sides about the axis from straight down. In a segment's frame a room is a box like any other: x across, z along the ship, its deck's floor at y = -floorR. Each deck has a ring corridor (`corridor`, z) with rooms fore and aft of it (`rows`). The spokes run from the corridors in their segments up to the hub ring, which turns round the fixed spine at `hub.r`. Outside the decks is the belt (water tanks and stores, spinning), then a gap, then the fixed sleeve.

hub.transfer: Catch the hub ring at walking pace; a spin-matched car takes stretchers and cargo.

fighter.about: One fighter, flown (src/carrier/fighter.mjs): the same thruster physics as the carrier, in the fighter's own frame. Built for vacuum (tools/blender/fighter_build.py): a crew capsule, two propellant tanks, radiators that fold up instead of wings; `size` is her box without the radiators, which weigh little. 12 t; the main drive gives about 3 g, the manoeuvring clusters about 1 g sideways and a 180° turn in about 2 s. `thrusters` places the Blender model's thruster quads and the main drive's force; how she actually flies (the nozzles that push, the tanks, the attitude hold) is `flight`. `landing.lane`: how far out the approach lane's rings run; `ring` their radius; `catch` how close to the gate (m along, m off the line sideways and up) and how slow (m/s) flight control catches a fighter you fly in yourself.

g.about: What g does to the pilot (src/carrier/gload.mjs). Shift with W is hard burn: the drive's push rises to `boost` times its rating over `spool` seconds, burning propellant to match. Past `tolerate` g the pilot's strain builds at `onset` a second for every g over (times `juiceCut` while the couch's `juice` lasts, seconds of it, topped up on the pad); at 1 she blacks out until it falls back under 0.45; under `tolerate` it falls at `recover` a second.

flight.about: How she flies (src/carrier/flight.mjs), as signed off in the Fighter Sound Lab: Newton only, no drag, no top speed, no drift kill. `hold`: the drive lights at `rampFrom` of full power and ramps at `rampRate` a second while W is held; the aim may lead the nose by `lead` rad; `sens` rad a mouse pixel; `keyRate` / `rollRate` the turn the arrows and Z C ask for (rad/s); `wmax` the hold's cruise turn rate per axis (pitch, yaw, roll); `minPop` the smallest pop as a fraction of a second of full jets; `gap` the beat between pops. `inertia` (kg m²) and `com` in her model's frame. `blocks`: the four jet blocks (bow and stern at the height of the centre of mass, so a slide is a pure slide and a yaw a pure yaw), `pan` for the sound. `nozzles`: [id, block, the way the gas goes, `force` kind, metres out from the block]. `alloc`: per command (slide right, rise, back (retro), pitch up, yaw left, roll left) the nozzles each way. `opposed`: pairs that would cancel, so neither opens. `tank` kg and `isp` s: 3 t of torch-drive propellant and 1.2 t of cold gas (about 250 m/s of sliding). `nozzle`: the drive's mouth.

routes.about: Wayfinding (src/carrier/wayfinding.mjs): each route is a coloured line painted along the floor of every passage, with arrows, that turns off through the door on the way to `to`. The overhead signs and the deck plans use the same colours.

damage.about: Damage control jobs (src/carrier/damage.mjs). When a hit hurts a room (see `integrity.jobs`), something goes wrong there: the ship's speakers call it out with its place (deck, frame, side) and you go and deal with it. `first` and `between` are the seconds before the first job and between jobs. `kits` is what you carry: `lockers` puts it in cabinets along every passage, `rooms` in a rack just inside those rooms. Each kind needs its `kit`, `work` seconds of holding E, and maybe `isolate` (at a room in `switchboards` first). A fire grows every `grows` seconds and is lost at size `lost`; an electrical fault left live becomes `becomes` after `after` seconds; a leak is lost after `lost` seconds. `rooms` limits where a kind can happen (`passages` for the corridors).

weapons.about: The carrier's guns, her point defence and her torpedoes, and the raider that attacks her (src/carrier/weapons.mjs). There are no shields: what keeps a ship alive is armour (`integrity.armour`), point defence, and not being where the shot is aimed. `turrets`: each heavy turret is a `mount` (its id, also the name of its gunhouse in hull.glb, and `<id>-guns` its barrels), fed from its `magazine` compartment up its `barbette`; `from` is the hatch you man it from (deck, spot, the way you face when you leave). `gun`, for every turret: `shell` muzzle speed m/s, `reload` seconds per barrel, `crewReload` the same for a turret its crew fires, `train` and `elevate` the fastest it turns (degrees a second), `elevation` its limits (degrees, toward the side the turret stands on), `rack` rounds in the ready rack, `stock` rounds in the magazine, `hoist` seconds to send one round up, `spread` the aim error of a shot (radians), `crewSpread` how far off a crew lays the guns, `range` metres a shell flies, `damage` what one does to the raider's hull, `fouled` metres of line of fire checked against the hull, `heat` what one shot puts into the ship's heat sinks (0 to 1 of them). `pdc`: the point defence cannons, rotary guns on the layout's `pdc` mounts, run by the fire-control computer: each one takes the nearest torpedo (or, with none, the raider inside `raiderRange`) that is within `range` and `arc` degrees of where the mount faces, leads it (for its acceleration too), slews at `slew` degrees a second and fires `rate` tracers a second (each tracer stands for a burst of rounds) at `speed` m/s, off by `spread` radians; a tracer passing within `radius` metres of a torpedo kills it, and one that meets the raider does `damage`. `stock` is the tracers each mount's magazine holds (its `magazine` in the mounts), `heat` what each tracer puts into the sinks. A mount is as healthy as the compartment it is fixed to. `torpedo`: every torpedo, either side's: `accel` m/s² for `burn` seconds, launched at `push` m/s, gone after `life` seconds; `jink` m/s² of random weave once it is within `terminal` metres (what makes point defence miss); `fuse` metres from its target it goes off. Into the carrier it does `pen`, `damage` and `hole` as a shell does (integrity.mjs), never stopped by the armour; into the raider, `raiderDamage`. `tubes`: the carrier's own torpedo tubes, fired by the CIC at a raider between `range` metres: `salvo` at a time, `every` seconds, from `magazine` while it holds `stock`, out of the hull at `at` (ship frame) along `dir`. `raider`: its `hull` (armour and all), `speed` (m/s past the carrier) and `accel`, `jink` (m/s² of evasive weave, changing every second or two: what makes a long shot miss), `standoff` (the range of its passes, metres), `passes`, `size` (half-axes of the ellipsoid shells hit), its `gun` (`shell` m/s, seconds `every` between shots, `spread`, `range`), its `torpedo` launches (a `salvo` every `every` seconds while the carrier is between `range` metres, `stock` in all), its own point defence `pdc` against the carrier's torpedoes (`range`, `rate`, `spread`, `speed`), and its `flak` at a fighter within `range`: a shot `every` so many seconds at `shell` m/s, aimed where she will be if she flies on as she is, off by up to `spread` radians, doing `damage` if it passes within `radius` metres of her. `target`: the gunnery drill's sled, towed `tow` metres astern of a tug on `passes` straight passes `standoff` metres off at `speed`; `size` is the ellipsoid a shell must pass through to score, `clear` how far off the tug is gone. It has no hull to lose: hits are counted. `fighter`: the fighter's twin cannon: `shell` m/s on top of her own velocity, seconds `every` between rounds, `spread`, `range` metres a round flies, `rounds` in the drum (refilled on the pad), the `damage` one round does to a raider (or a torpedo, within `radius`), and her own `hull` (mended on the pad; at nothing she is dead in space and flight control brings her in). `railgun`: the spinal gun along the keel, fired from the helm (F): it points where the ship points, so you aim it by turning her. A slug leaves at `speed` m/s on top of her velocity, off by `spread`; the capacitors take `charge` seconds to fill (on main power only) and each shot puts `heat` into the sinks; a slug that meets the raider does `damage`, and it is gone after `range` metres. `stock` slugs; the muzzle is at `muzzle` (ship frame).

broadside.about: The hangar walls' torpedo tubes, launched cold sideways: `per` a side, each side fed from its two ordnance rooms.

integrity.about: What hits do to the ship (src/carrier/integrity.mjs). Every compartment is a volume of air (kPa) with a health. `air`: `nominal` pressure; pressure doors close when either side falls below `doorsShut`, and open by hand only if the two sides are within `openWithin`; below `unsafe` a room shows as without air, below `faint` you black out after `blackout` seconds; `falling` is the kPa a second that counts as losing air; life support puts back `refill` kPa a second; `through` is how freely air passes an open doorway (m/s); `wind` the fastest you are pulled toward a hole. `hole.flow` is how fast air leaves through a hole to space (m/s, about the speed of sound's share in choked flow). `shell`: the ranges a hit is dealt from: `pen` metres through the ship, `damage` health taken, `hole` area in m². `drones` seal holes: `count` of them in the `from` room, `speed` m/s, `seal` seconds for a 0.1 m² hole, `inside` whether they also seal holes between compartments. `patch.work` is the seconds of holding E to patch a hole yourself. Below `power.below` of reactor health the ship is on emergency power. `attack`: seconds to the first and between raids, how many hits in one, the seconds of warning, and the seconds after the last hit before the ship stands down from action stations (all pressure doors are kept shut until then). `jobs`: the chance a damaging hit starts a fire, an electrical fault or a coolant leak, and the health a finished job puts back. `armour`: the belt round her; a gun shell is stopped by it (a scar, no hole) `stop` of the time, and one that gets through has lost `pen` metres (a torpedo is never stopped). `condition`: condition one, set at action stations: `warn` seconds after the call, the air in every walkable compartment is pumped down to `to` kPa at `pump` kPa a second (into the tanks, not lost), so a hit cannot blow a room out or start a fire; after the stand-down it comes back at `repress` kPa a second. Everyone suits up first. `suit`: a vac suit (the `suit` kit, worn, not carried) holds `air` seconds of breathing, warns at `low`, and takes `don` seconds to put on; with your helmet on, the room's air does not matter to you.

plant.about: The ship's plant (src/carrier/plant.mjs): her heat and her reaction mass. Heat is how full her heat sinks are, 0 to 1 (`heat`): the reactor puts in `base` a second at idle and `drive` more at full main drive; weapons put in what their own `heat` says. The radiators (the layout's `radiator` mounts) take out up to `reject` a second when fully spread and the sinks full (less as the sinks cool), as much as they are spread and unhurt; folded they still shed `folded` of that. They fold and spread in `deploy` seconds, and the ship folds them herself at action stations (`foldAtStations`). The sinks hold less as the heat sink compartments are hurt. Above `warn` the ship calls a heat warning; at `limit` the point defence and the railgun hold their fire (the turrets' crews keep firing) and the main drive is held to `throttle`. `propellant`: `mass` kg of reaction mass at the start, in the `tanks` compartments (shared by volume), burned by the main drive at `isp` seconds; an open hole in a tank compartment loses `leak` of that tank's share a second.
